title: 2D Lists
objective: Create and access a list of lists (a 2D list) to model grid-like data such as rows and columns.

sourceAlignment.title: Python Full Course for free
sourceAlignment.creator: Bro Code
sourceAlignment.note: Alignment metadata only; this topic isn't covered in Python Crash Course but is taught in the companion video. Lesson prose and exercises are original Code Forge material.

paragraphs: A 2D list is a list whose elements are themselves lists — think of it as a grid, where the outer list holds the rows and each inner list holds one row's values. grid = [[1, 2], [3, 4]] describes a 2-row, 2-column grid.

To reach a single value, use two indices in a row: grid[0] gives you the first inner list (the first row), and grid[0][1] gives you the second value within that row. The first index picks the row, the second picks the position within that row.

Looping over a 2D list usually means nesting two for loops: the outer loop visits each row (each inner list), and the inner loop visits each value within that row — the exact nested-loop pattern from the last lesson, applied to real data instead of a range.
explanation.rule: grid[row][col] reaches a single value in a 2D list — the first index picks which inner list, the second picks the position inside it.

examples.title: Reading a Grid
examples.note: grid[0] is the whole first row, [1, 2, 3]. grid[0][1] narrows down to a single value within that row: 2.

assignment.title: Grid Total

requirements: Use a nested loop to visit every value in every row.
Accumulate the total with += and return it.
